differential: von Willebrand Disease Type 1

Decreased vWF antigen, reduced ristocetin cofactor activity, and mildly decreased Factor VIII with mucocutaneous bleeding and family history are pathognomonic for this most common inherited bleeding disorder.
von Willebrand Disease Type 2
Qualitative vWF defects can present with reduced ristocetin cofactor activity disproportionate to vWF antigen levels, though the concurrent low vWF antigen makes Type 1 more likely.
von Willebrand Disease Type 3
Though this severe form presents with very low vWF levels, the patient's ability to function into adulthood with only menorrhagia and easy bruising makes this less likely than milder forms.
Mild Hemophilia A (carrier state)
Reduced Factor VIII can cause similar bleeding symptoms, but the decreased vWF antigen and ristocetin cofactor activity point more specifically to von Willebrand disease.
Combined Factor VIII and vWF deficiency
Rare inherited conditions can affect both factors simultaneously, though this is typically part of the von Willebrand disease spectrum rather than a separate entity.
